articles.title: Devs are inspecting Greenhouse payloads to find hidden salary caps
articles.excerpt: Next time a job portal asks for your "desired salary," just open your DevTools and you might find the answer sitting right in the payload. Recently, developers have been peeping into application forms…
articles.body: Next time a job portal asks for your "desired salary," just open your DevTools and you might find the answer sitting right in the payload. Recently, developers have been peeping into application forms. The JSON they hide says far more than the recruiter ever will. 🕵️ The field that pretends to ask Here's how it goes. You complete an application on a platform such as Greenhouse. There is a box that says: "What are your salary expectations?" It seems non-threatening. It seems like a direct question. No, it's not. Pop open the network tab, watch the request fire, and sometimes you'll spot a number the form never showed you. An upper limit. A maximum threshold. The actual budget hidden in the reply.
articles.author: Aditya Agarwal

articles.body: You see the screenshots everywhere: architecture maps that light up a request path on click, fade everything else back, and let you walk a system layer by layer. They come from Archify — the open-source diagram project on GitHub (tt-a1i/archify), MIT-licensed — which has collected more than 65,000 stars since April 2026 (as of September 2026). Then you open the repository and hit the catch: Archify is not a website. It is an agent skill and a CLI, meant to live inside Claude Code, Codex, or a similar tool. Most people searching for "Archify online" want the maps, not the tooling around them.

articles.title: Why on Earth Does the Claude Logo Still Look Like a Sphincter?
articles.excerpt: I need to talk about the Claude logo. Seriously. It's 6 in the morning on a random Monday and this thought won't leave my brain. Not the model. Not Anthropic. Not constitutional AI, safety research, c…
articles.body: I need to talk about the Claude logo. Seriously. It's 6 in the morning on a random Monday and this thought won't leave my brain. Not the model. Not Anthropic. Not constitutional AI, safety research, context windows, coding benchmarks, agents, MCP servers, or whatever new thing Claude can now do with your entire filesystem. The logo. Because somehow, in an industry currently spending billions of dollars attempting to create artificial general intelligence, nobody has solved the much simpler problem of: why does Claude's logo look like an anus? I'm sorry. It does. And once somebody points this out to you, there is no going back. Did the logo designer accidentally paste an asterisk from their handoff notes into the final email? You can call it a sunburst. You can call it an asterisk.

articles.title: Handbrake Alternatives: What to Use When You Don't Want to Install It
articles.excerpt: People look for a Handbrake alternative for one of three reasons, and they need different answers. Some want the same power without the interface — they're fine installing software, they just find Han…
articles.body: People look for a Handbrake alternative for one of three reasons, and they need different answers. Some want the same power without the interface — they're fine installing software, they just find Handbrake's settings panel unfriendly. Some want no install at all , usually because it's one file, or a work laptop that won't allow it, or a phone. And some want something Handbrake can't do — editing, trimming, subtitles, format conversions outside its range. Worth saying clearly first: for batch-processing a library with precise encoder control, Handbrake is still the best free option and nothing listed below beats it at that. This is about the jobs where it's more tool than the task needs. Browser-based compressors The category that barely existed a few years ago.

articles.body: Introduction Currently, we are working on many products infused with AI across the company . Instead of relying solely on a harness to provide AI agents with tools, context, memory, and other capabilities to make them smarter and more aware of the environments in which they operate, we also need the ability to evaluate these agents and provide feedback so they can continuously improve. We have researched and experimented with several AI evaluation platforms, including Arize Phoenix , Microsoft Foundry , and Langfuse . After evaluating them against our requirements and roadmap, we shortlisted Microsoft Foundry and Langfuse because they fit well with our company's direction. Let's start with Langfuse in this post, and we will cover Microsoft Foundry in a future post.

articles.title: Resize and strip EXIF metadata from user uploads in Node.js
articles.excerpt: If your app lets users upload images, two things are almost certainly true and Those photos carry EXIF metadata — including, for anything shot on a phone, the GPS coordinates of where it was taken. Se…
articles.body: If your app lets users upload images, two things are almost certainly true and almost certainly ignored: Those photos carry EXIF metadata — including, for anything shot on a phone, the GPS coordinates of where it was taken. Serve the original file and you're broadcasting your users' home addresses. They're huge . A modern phone photo is 3–8 MB. Ship those to visitors untouched and your pages crawl and your bandwidth bill climbs. The fix for both is the same pass: resize, re-compress, convert to a modern format, and strip the metadata. Here's how to do it properly in Node — and where the sharp edges are, because there are a few that bite people in production. The DIY version with sharp sharp (libvips under the hood) is the right tool.

articles.excerpt: Tests point to a router-specific sleep issue, but the cause isn't confirmed.
articles.body: TL;DR Some Pixel 11 owners are reporting excessive idle battery drain, with Wi-Fi showing unusually high battery usage. A detailed test found that certain routers repeatedly woke the phone, preventing it from sleeping properly. Switching to Wi-Fi 5 or another router dramatically improved battery life, but the exact cause remains unconfirmed. Pixel owners are no strangers to battery-life complaints , and Google’s Tensor era has had its share of heat, modem, and efficiency problems. The Pixel 11 series looked like a step forward, especially with its new MediaTek modem, but some owners are now chasing a different kind of drain. A detailed Reddit investigation suggests certain Wi-Fi routers may be keeping Pixel 11 phones awake far more often than they should.

articles.title: Silent Hill: Townfall Review
articles.excerpt: Like the intravenous needle permanently jutting out of its hero’s wrist, Silent Hill: Townfall gives this long running series a welcome shot in the arm.
articles.body: I spent so much of my time stalking through Silent Hill: Townfall tensed in a cautious crouchwalk, that by the end of the story I was just as worried about the damage to my character’s fraying mental state as I was about the wear and tear on his knees. Taking an about-face from the action-heavy adventure in last year’s Silent Hill f, this latest survival horror spin-off instead embraces the sustained tension of slow-paced stealth, handing you a motion-sensing gadget and tasking you with sneaking past a series of sound-sensitive beasts that have descended on its abandoned seaside village in mid-nineties Scotland. What unfolds is a gripping investigation through an increasingly unsettling world witnessed from a fresh, first-person perspective.
